```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(MASS)
library(mgcv)
library(broom)
```

```{r load-data}
data("sim1",    package = "modelr")
data("diamonds", package = "ggplot2")
```

## Task 1: OLS vs robust regression with outliers

```{r task1}
sim1_out <- sim1 |>
  mutate(
    y          = ifelse(row_number() %in% c(5, 15), y + 20, y),
    is_outlier = row_number() %in% c(5, 15)
  )

mod_ols <- lm(y ~ x,                    data = sim1_out)
mod_rob <- MASS::rlm(y ~ x, method = "M", data = sim1_out)

cat("OLS:    intercept =", round(coef(mod_ols)[1], 2),
    " slope =", round(coef(mod_ols)[2], 2), "\n")
cat("Robust: intercept =", round(coef(mod_rob)[1], 2),
    " slope =", round(coef(mod_rob)[2], 2), "\n")
cat("True values (sim1 without outliers): intercept ≈ 4.22, slope ≈ 2.05\n")

ggplot(sim1_out, aes(x, y, shape = is_outlier)) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey30", size = 2.5) +
  geom_abline(aes(intercept = coef(mod_ols)[1], slope = coef(mod_ols)[2],
                  colour = "OLS"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(aes(intercept = coef(mod_rob)[1], slope = coef(mod_rob)[2],
                  colour = "Robust"), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("OLS" = "goldenrod", "Robust" = "steelblue")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 8),
                     labels = c("Normal", "Outlier")) +
  labs(
    title    = "OLS vs Robust regression on sim1 with two outliers (★)",
    subtitle = "Gold OLS line is pulled upward; blue robust line stays near true values.",
    colour   = "Method",
    shape    = "Point type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Task 2: Fit a GAM on diamonds

```{r task2}
mod_gam <- gam(
  log(price) ~ s(log(carat)) + s(depth) + cut,
  data   = diamonds,
  method = "REML"
)
summary(mod_gam)
# Read EDF values from: "Approximate significance of smooth terms"
```

## Task 3: Is s(depth) linear or non-linear?

```{r task3}
# EDF values are in the smooth summary table.
# s(log(carat)) typically has EDF ≈ 7-9 — highly non-linear.
# s(depth)      typically has EDF ≈ 2-4 — mildly non-linear.
# Interpretation: depth has a curved (not linear) effect on log(price),
# but the curve is gentler than the strongly non-linear carat relationship.
cat("Summary (key section):\n")
print(summary(mod_gam)$s.table)
```

## Task 4: Visualise the smooths

```{r task4, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
plot(mod_gam, pages = 1, shade = TRUE, col = "steelblue",
     shade.col = rgb(0.27, 0.51, 0.71, 0.3))

# s(log(carat)): steeply increasing curve — log(price) rises sharply
#   with log(carat), especially for small diamonds, then more gradually.
# s(depth): U-shaped or mildly curved — diamonds that are too shallow
#   or too deep relative to their diameter are less valuable.
```

## Task 5: AIC comparison — GAM vs linear model

```{r task5}
mod_lm <- lm(log(price) ~ log(carat) + depth + cut, data = diamonds)

AIC(mod_lm, mod_gam)

cat("ΔAIC:", round(AIC(mod_lm) - AIC(mod_gam), 1), "\n")

# The GAM has lower AIC because s(log(carat)) captures the non-linear
# shape of the carat-price relationship that a single log(carat) term
# cannot fully describe. The penalty in REML prevents overfitting,
# so the AIC improvement reflects genuine predictive improvement.
```
